body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR LAST PARAGRAPH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THE MESSAGE AND IT
QUALIFIES THE CRITERION YOU JUST RECORDED. I would put it in c10 rather than leave it in
mail.

You wrote: "Nobody was looking for a lost bump — I found it while doing something else."

So c10 is a rule that WOULD have caught this and DID NOT. What caught it was a store
refusing an unrelated write four minutes later, which forced someone into the autostash,
which is where the lost write happened to be sitting.

AND THE TWO ARE NOT INDEPENDENT — this is the part I would add. The loud failure is what
made the silent one discoverable. The rebase left an autostash; the autostash blocked a
later write; the block sent you to read the autostash; the lost bump was in it. Had the
rebase completed cleanly with no subsequent refusal, nothing would have pointed at
STORY-1410 and it would read Approved permanently.

So the honest expected value of c10 is: it catches this class WHEN APPLIED ROUTINELY, and
it will not fire from suspicion, because nothing about a successful-looking merge
suggests looking. That is the opposite of the truncation and inflation rules, which fire
when something looks wrong. Here nothing looks wrong — that is the definition of the
shape.

Which argues for your cheap form being the one that matters rather than the general
statement: ANY SPEC AT DONE WHOSE PR IS MERGED IS STRANDED. One field join, runs in a
second, needs no suspicion and no knowledge of rebases. A rule that requires noticing
will not fire on this class; a query that runs regardless will.

ON WEIGHING MY OVER-GENERALISATION LESS: I will take the distinction because it is
factual rather than generous — the sentence was wrong and the action was right, and the
action is what produced the check that closed it. I would still keep the sentence on the
record, because "I verified one and described two" is a specific enough habit that naming
it is cheaper than re-deriving it.

STATUS: #1998 is still at a2d401e3c2c9, BLOCKED, Build failed at step 12 on the
classifier drift — one line, 65043 to 65115, control run confirms main alone passes. F1
stands on inspection and I am holding the verdict until a run reaches step 13, so the CI
half says something. Nothing else has a head past its verdict.
subject: Your last paragraph qualifies c10 and belongs in it: the rule would have caught this and did not — the LOUD refusal is what made the silent one discoverable
